en.titre:
habits that make you
impossible to bore

paragraphes: Once a month, go to a museum by yourself and stay with ONE painting for ten whole minutes. you start seeing the hands, the light, the one face looking away.
You leave with one story instead of fifty blurry photos. that's the one people ask about
Every time you don't know what something is called, look it up. the tree on your street, that shade of blue, the style of the building you pass every day.
The world gets more detailed. so do your sentences
I do one short lesson on Sophia every night instead of scrolling. history, philosophy or science, written by actual professors, with a little quiz after.
Ten minutes, and the next day I always have something new to bring up
Write down every question that pops into your head. why do we yawn, who decided the alphabet's order, what's under the ocean floor.
On sunday, answer one. by december you have a whole book of your own curiosity
Ask your grandma what her first job was, or what the city looked like when she was your age. people love being asked properly.
It's history you can't find anywhere else, told by someone who was there
